### AgentAppearance

```ts
type AgentAppearance = Readonly<{
  cap: string;
  capSpot: string;
}>;
```

The mushroom's two identity controls for one seed: its cap and cap spots take a
hue from the seed, so an Agent wears the same cap in every list it appears in.
Kept byte-identical to the Sprite seen before avatars existed.

### avatarEnvelopeSchema

```ts
const avatarEnvelopeSchema: ZodObject<
  {
    v: ZodLiteral<1>;
    character: ZodEnum<{
      mushroom: "mushroom";
      cat: "cat";
      burger: "burger";
    }>;
    appearance: ZodRecord<
      ZodString,
      ZodUnion<readonly [ZodString, ZodNumber, ZodBoolean]>
    >;
    expression: ZodString;
    renderStyle: ZodEnum<{
      plain: "plain";
      pencil: "pencil";
      manga: "manga";
      riso: "riso";
      halftone: "halftone";
      blueprint: "blueprint";
      crt: "crt";
      watercolor: "watercolor";
    }>;
  },
  $strict
>;
```

The Avatar v1 envelope: a closed character, up to 16 appearance values, a
resting expression, and a render style. It is a complete snapshot, not a
reference into character data, so it survives a later change to the catalog.
This checks shape only; it does not know a character's real controls or
expressions, so a bound catalog cannot validate against it by name alone.
`createAvatarSchema`/`parseAvatar` build the catalog-refined schema a caller
should actually parse untrusted data with; `sprite-zdog`'s `avatarSchema` is
that schema, bound to the built-in catalog.

```ts
function createAvatarSchema(catalog): ZodObject<
  {

      crt: "crt";
      watercolor: "watercolor";
    }>;
  },

```

Build the full avatar schema for a catalog: the envelope above, refined so every
appearance key is one of the character's controls, every value is typed by that
control, and the expression is one the character declares.

### agentHueStep()

```ts
function agentHueStep(hex, seed, avoid?): number;
```

The hue-rotation step for `seed`, chosen against `hex`'s own realised result,
not the idealised `hue + step` arithmetic: `shiftHue` rounds to a `#rrggbb`
colour, and re-decoding that colour can land a few tenths of a degree short of
an exact-degree step, which the 40-degree guarantee must still hold against. A
step is only a candidate when rotating `hex` by it and reading the result's hue
back out clears 40 degrees from `hex`'s own hue. When `avoid` carries other
agents' identity hues, the candidate farthest from all of them (by minimum
distance, scored on the same realised hue) is preferred; ties keep whichever
candidate is nearest the seed's own deterministic default step, so an
unconflicted seed keeps its usual look.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type                | Default value |
| --------- | ------------------- | ------------- |
| `hex`     | `string`            | `undefined`   |
| `seed`    | `string`            | `undefined`   |
| `avoid`   | readonly `number`[] | `[]`          |

#### Returns

`number`

### deriveAgentAvatar()

```ts
function deriveAgentAvatar(member, agentColors, seed, catalog, avoid?): object;
```

Derive an Agent's avatar from its creator's, for a catalog's character. `"keep"`
hands back the member's look unchanged (their Agent is a visible copy, told
apart only by name). `"shift"` resolves the member's full appearance against the
catalog and rotates only the character's identity slots by one shared hue step,
so accessories, face and drawing style carry over untouched. `avoid` lists hues
already worn by the creator's other Agents so a new one does not land beside
them. An achromatic primary identity colour has no hue to rotate, so its
resolved appearance is kept.
